citeAs: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li (2023). LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding. arXiv:2308.14508.
creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li (Tsinghua University, Zhipu.AI, Institute of Automation Chinese Academy of Sciences)
description: LongBench is the first bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding of large language models. It comprises 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese, with an average length of 6,711 words (English) and 13,386 characters (Chinese), covering single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion. It contains 4,750 test instances and supports fully automated evaluation using metrics such as ROUGE-L, F1, and Edit Similarity.
name: LongBench
rai:annotationsPerItem: For MultiFieldQA, each article was annotated by three Ph.D. students (one question-answer pair per annotator per article).
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators for MultiFieldQA are Ph.D. students with extensive research experience in the field of NLP, described as expert annotators.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cross-validation among annotators for MultiFieldQA shows a 100% accuracy rate of the annotated answers.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For MultiFieldQA datasets, three Ph.D. students were invited to annotate questions and answers for each article. Annotation guidelines required: (1) questions should be as clear as possible with definitive and relatively short answers; (2) the distribution of evidence paragraphs should be as random as possible throughout the article; (3) questions should have varied types including information-extracting, summarizing, and multi-hop reasoning questions. Annotators ensured answers could be inferred from the documents and that evidence placement was random to avoid positional biases. The average annotation time per sample was around 5 minutes.
rai:dataBiases: The authors explicitly acknowledged and designed against positional bias: evidence placement in MultiFieldQA was made as random as possible throughout the article to avoid biases that might occur if answer-related statements were frequently found at the beginning or end of documents. The authors also noted that memorization performance on HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, and MuSiQue is relatively high because these datasets are derived from Wikipedia, a common source for training prevalent LLMs, meaning models may rely on memorization rather than context understanding.
rai:dataCollection: LongBench datasets were collected through three approaches: (1) 6 datasets extracted directly from original public datasets (e.g., NarrativeQA, GovReport); (2) 10 datasets built and processed from existing datasets to be suitable for long context evaluation (e.g., HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, DuReader, QMSum, MultiNews, TREC, TriviaQA, SAMSum, LSHT); and (3) 5 datasets created and annotated by the authors (MultiFieldQA-en, MultiFieldQA-zh, PassageCount, PassageRetrieval-en, PassageRetrieval-zh). For multi-doc QA, complete Wikipedia passages were used as context with supporting and distracting passages randomly ordered. For few-shot tasks, examples were randomly sampled from training sets. For synthetic tasks, passages were randomly sampled from Wikipedia and C4 dataset.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data includes: literature and film scripts (NarrativeQA), NLP papers (Qasper), legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, academic papers from Arxiv, C4 Dataset, WuDaoCorpora, Chinese Judgements Online, Wikipedia, and Chinese Government Website (MultiFieldQA), Wikipedia-based multi-hop QA datasets (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue), Baidu Search and Baidu Zhidao (DuReader), U.S. Government Accountability Office and Congressional Research Service reports (GovReport), meeting transcripts (QMSum, VCSUM), news articles (MultiNews, LSHT), web questions (TREC), Wikipedia and web (TriviaQA), messenger-like dialogues (SAMSum), English Wikipedia and Chinese C4 dataset (PassageRetrieval), GitHub code repositories (LCC, RepoBench-P).
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
rai:dataLimitations: (1) Potentially unreliable automatic metrics: automatic evaluation metrics (ROUGE-L, F1) may not accurately reflect the quality of responses, and results may be underestimated for models that generate longer responses. (2) Coupling with instruction-following capabilities: performance on LongBench is coupled with models' instruction-following capabilities, making it difficult to purely assess long-context modeling ability. (3) Models may have encountered long context during pre-training and may rely on memorization rather than context understanding to answer questions, particularly for Wikipedia-derived datasets.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Two sampling strategies were used: (1) Random sampling to maintain a natural length distribution (producing LongBench); (2) Uniform sampling based on data length to produce an even distribution across length ranges of 0-4k, 4k-8k, and 8k+ words (producing LongBench-E). For PassageRetrieval tasks, one passage was selected for summarization using GPT-3.5-Turbo to create the query. For PassageCount, passages were randomly sampled from Wikipedia, each repeated a random number of times, and then shuffled.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For multi-doc QA tasks, complete Wikipedia passages encompassing supporting or distracting paragraphs were used as context; supporting passages were included first, then distracting passages were added until reaching a maximum length, and passages were randomly ordered. For DuReader, each question was associated with several related documents plus arbitrarily selected distractors until 20 documents total. For few-shot tasks, a random integer was selected as the number of examples, then corresponding samples were randomly drawn from training sets and concatenated. For code completion (RepoBench-P), cross-file code snippets were shuffled and combined with preceding lines of code. All 21 datasets were standardized into a unified (I, C, A) format. Data was extracted from test sets of public datasets to avoid test leakage (except VCSUM due to insufficient test data).
rai:dataSocialImpact: LongBench enables more rigorous evaluation of LLMs' long context understanding capabilities, facilitating further research in long context modeling. By providing a comprehensive bilingual benchmark, it supports the development of LLMs that can handle longer inputs such as books, reports, and codebases, which has broad applications in real-world NLP tasks.
rai:dataUseCases: LongBench is intended for evaluating large language models' long context understanding capabilities across multiple tasks and languages. It serves as a testbed for benchmarking LLMs on single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion in both English and Chinese. LongBench-E is specifically designed for studying how model performance changes across different context lengths within the same task.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5-Turbo was used to generate summaries of passages for the PassageRetrieval-en and PassageRetrieval-zh synthetic tasks (each passage was summarized using GPT-3.5-Turbo to create the query for the retrieval task).
